The invention relates to a mobile network subscriber intended for use in a cabled network. In particular, the invention is suitable for use in a collector wire network of an electric telpher or similar electrically powered transport system in which a mobile unit travels along a predefined path while maintaining electrical and data communication with stationary network infrastructure.

The cabled network comprises at least a first network segment and a second network segment. These segments may be arranged successively along the travel path of the mobile subscriber and may form part of a larger segmented communication network. Each segment can be connected to, or associated with, one or more master modems that provide communication access to the network.

The mobile network subscriber comprises two slave modems and two contact arrangements. Each slave modem is operatively connected to a respective contact arrangement. The contact arrangements are designed to establish electrical contact with the cabled network, for example with collector wires or conductor rails, so that data signals can be exchanged between the slave modems and the master modem or modems assigned to the respective network segments.

During operation, the slave modems communicate with one or more master modems via the contact arrangements and the corresponding network segments. In this way, the mobile network subscriber can remain connected to the communication network while moving along the cabled network. The use of two slave modems and two contact arrangements allows the mobile subscriber to maintain communication even when it moves from one network segment to another.

The contact arrangements are configured and positioned such that, during a transition from the first segment to the second segment, one of the contact arrangements remains electrically connected to the first segment while the other contact arrangement is already electrically connected to the second segment. As a result, the mobile network subscriber can establish communication with the second segment before completely losing communication with the first segment. This overlapping contact condition enables a smooth handover between network segments and reduces or prevents interruptions in communication during travel across segment boundaries.

Thus, the invention provides a mobile network subscriber that is particularly well suited for segmented cabled networks, such as collector wire networks of electric telphers, where reliable communication must be maintained while the subscriber is in motion.
outputs.L4:
A mobile network subscriber intended for use in a cabled network, for example in an electric telpher collector wire network, is equipped to maintain reliable data communication while it travels along the network. The network may be divided into a plurality of separate line or cable segments, each of which is associated with at least one master modem. In order to communicate with these master modems, the mobile subscriber includes two slave modems and two separate contact arrangements, such as sliding contacts, current collectors, or similar contacting devices. Each slave modem is connected to one of the contact arrangements so that the subscriber can establish communication through different portions of the cable network as it moves.

During normal operation, one contact arrangement engages a first network segment and the corresponding slave modem communicates with the master modem assigned to that segment. As the mobile subscriber approaches a transition point between two adjacent segments, the second contact arrangement can make contact with the next network segment while the first contact arrangement is still connected to the preceding segment. In this condition, both network segments can be contacted at the same time, at least temporarily, and the two slave modems can operate independently with the respective master modems of the two segments.

This configuration allows the mobile subscriber to transfer communication from one segment to the next in a simple and efficient manner. Since the first contact arrangement remains connected to the first segment until the second contact arrangement has already established a connection with the second segment, interruption of communication can be avoided or greatly reduced. The mobile subscriber can therefore continue to exchange data with the network while crossing the boundary between segments.

The use of two slave modems and two contact arrangements also simplifies the control of the transition. Instead of requiring a complex switching mechanism or a precisely timed changeover, the subscriber can maintain an existing communication link through one modem while preparing or establishing the next communication link through the other modem. Once communication over the second segment is available and stable, the subscriber may release the connection to the first segment and continue operation through the second segment.

Such an arrangement is particularly advantageous in transport systems in which vehicles or carriers move along an electrified or wired path and require continuous communication for control, monitoring, positioning, safety functions, or data exchange. By ensuring that at least one contact remains connected to an active segment during the transition between adjacent segments, the system provides robust communication continuity with relatively simple hardware and without requiring extensive interruption-tolerant protocols.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” may be one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, but it plays an important role in communication. It helps us identify something specific, turning a general idea into a clear reference. For example, “a book” could mean any book, but “the book” points to one particular book that the speaker and listener both understand.

Because of this, “the” gives language precision. It connects people through shared knowledge and context. Whether we say “the sun,” “the world,” or “the future,” this simple word helps shape meaning and direction.

Although it is often overlooked, “the” is essential in everyday speech and writing. It reminds us that even the smallest words can carry great importance.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent abstract for a mobile network subscriber in a cabled collector wire network for an electric telpher, using reference numerals for segments, slave modems, master modems, and contact arrangements.
counterfactuals.output: A mobile network subscriber for an electric telpher system is provided for communication over a cabled collector wire network. The collector wire network is divided into electrically defined segments (10, 12, 14), each segment being associated with at least one stationary master modem (20, 22, 24) coupled to the respective segment. A telpher vehicle carries a mobile subscriber unit (30) including a slave modem (32) connected to current-collector contact arrangements (40, 42) that engage the collector wires of the active segment. The slave modem (32) communicates data signals with the master modem (20, 22, 24) of the segment (10, 12, 14) presently contacted by the contact arrangements (40, 42), while power supply to the vehicle is maintained via the same or adjacent collector conductors. Upon travel of the telpher vehicle from one segment to a next segment, the contact arrangements (40, 42) establish conductive coupling to the next segment before or during release from the preceding segment, enabling transfer of communication between corresponding master modems (20, 22, 24). The arrangement permits continuous or substantially uninterrupted data communication with the mobile network subscriber (30) along the travel path of the electric telpher without requiring separate radio communication infrastructure.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a European-style patent claim/summary describing an invention that enables a mobile network node to switch efficiently between two cable network segments using two slave modems and two contact arrangements.
counterfactuals.output:
**Claim 1.** A mobile network node for operation on a cable-based communication network comprising at least a first cable network segment and a second cable network segment, the mobile network node comprising:

- a first slave modem configured for communication with the first cable network segment;
- a second slave modem configured for communication with the second cable network segment;
- a first contact arrangement associated with the first slave modem and configured to establish an electrical connection between the mobile network node and the first cable network segment;
- a second contact arrangement associated with the second slave modem and configured to establish an electrical connection between the mobile network node and the second cable network segment; and
- a control unit configured to control the first and second slave modems and the first and second contact arrangements,

wherein the control unit is configured, during movement of the mobile network node from the first cable network segment to the second cable network segment, to establish communication between the second slave modem and the second cable network segment via the second contact arrangement while communication between the first slave modem and the first cable network segment via the first contact arrangement is maintained, and subsequently to release the connection between the first contact arrangement and the first cable network segment, thereby enabling a transition between the first and second cable network segments with reduced interruption of network communication.

**Claim 2.** The mobile network node according to claim 1, wherein the control unit is configured to perform a registration, synchronisation, authentication or address allocation procedure for the second slave modem on the second cable network segment before disconnecting the first slave modem from the first cable network segment.

**Claim 3.** The mobile network node according to claim 1 or 2, wherein the first and second slave modems are operated at least temporarily in parallel during a handover interval.

**Claim 4.** The mobile network node according to any preceding claim, wherein the first and second contact arrangements are spaced apart in a direction of movement of the mobile network node such that, when the mobile network node passes a boundary between the first and second cable network segments, the second contact arrangement reaches the second cable network segment before the first contact arrangement leaves the first cable network segment.

**Claim 5.** The mobile network node according to any preceding claim, wherein each contact arrangement comprises one or more sliding contacts, brushes, rollers, collector shoes, inductive coupling elements, capacitive coupling elements or plug-in contact elements.

**Claim 6.** The mobile network node according to any preceding claim, wherein the control unit is configured to route user data traffic through the first slave modem before the transition and through the second slave modem after completion of the transition.

**Claim 7.** The mobile network node according to any preceding claim, wherein the control unit is configured to select one of the first and second slave modems as an active communication path based on signal quality, modem registration state, link availability or position information of the mobile network node.

**Claim 8.** The mobile network node according to any preceding claim, wherein the cable-based communication network is a broadband cable network, a coaxial network, an Ethernet-over-cable network or a power-line communication network.

**Claim 9.** A method for switching a mobile network node between a first cable network segment and a second cable network segment, the mobile network node comprising a first slave modem connected to a first contact arrangement and a second slave modem connected to a second contact arrangement, the method comprising:

- communicating with the first cable network segment by means of the first slave modem via the first contact arrangement;
- bringing the second contact arrangement into contact with the second cable network segment;
- establishing communication between the second slave modem and the second cable network segment while maintaining communication between the first slave modem and the first cable network segment;
- transferring communication of the mobile network node from the first slave modem to the second slave modem; and
- disconnecting the first contact arrangement from the first cable network segment after the second slave modem has established communication with the second cable network segment.

**Summary.**  
The invention relates to a mobile network node for a segmented cable communication system. The node is provided with two independently operable slave modems and two corresponding contact arrangements. As the node moves from one cable segment to a next cable segment, the leading contact arrangement connects to the next segment and the associated slave modem establishes communication with that segment while the other modem remains connected to the previous segment. After the new communication link is available, network traffic is transferred to the second modem and the previous contact is disconnected. This make-before-break operation reduces handover time and communication interruption when the mobile node passes between cable network segments.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a patent-style description of a mobile subscriber (10) moving along segments S1 and S2 of a cabled network (1), where contact arrangements K1 and K2 maintain communication with master modems during segment transition.
counterfactuals.output:
A mobile subscriber (10) is configured to communicate over a cabled network (1) while moving along a predetermined travel path comprising at least a first segment S1 and a second segment S2. The cabled network (1) comprises at least one communication cable extending along the travel path and a plurality of contact arrangements, including a first contact arrangement K1 associated with the first segment S1 and a second contact arrangement K2 associated with the second segment S2.

The mobile subscriber (10) comprises a subscriber-side modem and a contact unit configured to establish an electrical and/or signal-transmitting connection with the contact arrangements K1, K2 as the mobile subscriber (10) moves along the cabled network (1). The contact arrangements K1 and K2 are arranged such that, during movement of the mobile subscriber (10) from the first segment S1 to the second segment S2, communication with the cabled network (1) is maintained without interruption or with only negligible interruption.

In one embodiment, the first contact arrangement K1 is assigned to a first master modem associated with the first segment S1, and the second contact arrangement K2 is assigned to a second master modem associated with the second segment S2. While the mobile subscriber (10) travels within the first segment S1, the subscriber-side modem communicates with the first master modem via the first contact arrangement K1. As the mobile subscriber (10) approaches a transition region between the segments S1 and S2, the subscriber-side contact unit enters into contact with the second contact arrangement K2 while contact with the first contact arrangement K1 is still present or while communication via the first contact arrangement K1 remains available.

The contact arrangements K1 and K2 may be arranged with an overlap region, a bridging region, or a handover region in which the mobile subscriber (10) is simultaneously or sequentially connectable to both the first and second master modems. In this manner, a handover of the communication connection from the first master modem to the second master modem may be performed before, during, or immediately after the mobile subscriber (10) passes from segment S1 into segment S2.

The handover may comprise detecting the presence of the mobile subscriber (10) at or near the transition region, establishing a communication link between the subscriber-side modem and the second master modem via the second contact arrangement K2, synchronizing or registering the subscriber-side modem with the second master modem, and subsequently releasing or deactivating the communication link with the first master modem via the first contact arrangement K1. Alternatively, the subscriber-side modem may maintain parallel communication links with both master modems for a defined transition interval.

The cabled network (1) may further comprise a control device connected to the master modems and configured to coordinate the handover between the first and second master modems. The control device may allocate communication resources, transfer addressing or session information, and ensure that data communication with the mobile subscriber (10) continues during movement across the segment boundary.

Accordingly, the mobile subscriber (10) can travel from segment S1 to segment S2 of the cabled network (1) while the contact arrangements K1 and K2 provide continuous or substantially continuous signal coupling to respective master modems. This permits reliable data transmission in applications in which the mobile subscriber (10) moves along an extended cabled infrastructure, such as conveying systems, rail-guided transport systems, storage and retrieval systems, production lines, cranes, elevators, or other mobile industrial installations.

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose an invention disclosure paragraph for a mobile network subscriber in an electric overhead conveyor/telpher collector wire network, including first and second slave modems, contact arrangements, and communication with master modems across two network segments.
counterfactuals.output: An electric overhead conveyor/telpher collector wire communication system is disclosed in which a mobile network subscriber travels along a collector wire network divided into at least first and second network segments, each segment being associated with a respective stationary master modem. The mobile network subscriber includes a first slave modem and a second slave modem, each coupled to a respective contact arrangement configured to make sliding or rolling electrical contact with one or more collector wires as the subscriber moves along the conveyor path. The first contact arrangement is positioned to communicate with the master modem of the first network segment via the first slave modem, while the second contact arrangement is positioned to communicate with the master modem of the second network segment via the second slave modem, thereby enabling the mobile subscriber to exchange data signals over the collector wires with one or both network segments. The slave modems may be operated selectively, redundantly, or in parallel, such that communication is maintained during travel between segments, including during a transition region in which the contact arrangements engage different collector-wire portions associated with different master modems. This arrangement permits reliable bidirectional data communication between the moving subscriber and stationary control equipment without requiring a continuous radio link or trailing cable.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create formal patent wording for a device that allows seamless changeover between a first segment and second segment of a wired network by connecting one contact arrangement to each segment during transition.
counterfactuals.output:
A network changeover device for providing substantially uninterrupted transfer of a wired network connection between a first network segment and a second network segment, the device comprising:

a first interface configured to be electrically coupled to the first network segment;

a second interface configured to be electrically coupled to the second network segment;

a common interface configured to be electrically coupled to network equipment to be transferred between the first and second network segments; and

a switching assembly comprising a contact arrangement movable between a first operating position, a transition position, and a second operating position,

wherein, in the first operating position, the contact arrangement electrically couples the common interface to the first interface;

wherein, in the second operating position, the contact arrangement electrically couples the common interface to the second interface; and

wherein, in the transition position, the contact arrangement maintains an electrical connection between the common interface and the first interface while establishing an electrical connection between the common interface and the second interface, thereby temporarily connecting the common interface to both the first network segment and the second network segment during changeover.

In one embodiment, the switching assembly is configured such that the electrical connection to the second network segment is established before the electrical connection to the first network segment is interrupted, thereby providing a make-before-break transition between the first and second network segments.

In another embodiment, the contact arrangement comprises a plurality of conductive contacts corresponding to respective conductors of the wired network, each conductive contact being arranged to connect a respective conductor of the common interface to a corresponding conductor of the first interface, the second interface, or both the first and second interfaces during the transition position.

The device may further comprise a controller configured to actuate the switching assembly according to a predetermined sequence, wherein the predetermined sequence includes maintaining simultaneous conductive engagement with the first and second network segments for a defined transition interval.

The device may be configured for use with twisted-pair Ethernet cabling, telephone wiring, serial communication wiring, industrial fieldbus wiring, or another multi-conductor wired network medium.
